column1: # Terms that define the host taxon. Replace this file to target a different one.
#   field : any Entrez field, e.g. "All Fields", "Organism", "Title"
#   use   : query  -> only used to retrieve records
#           name   -> only used to recognise host-named viruses (e.g. "shrimp" in a virus name)
# Choosing `use`. The name-side regex does two jobs: it keeps a virus in tier 1 when its own
# name carries a host term even though its family is listed as environmental in
# tier2_groups.tsv, and it accepts a record with no /host qualifier when the virus name names
# the host. Both depend on how viruses are actually named -- after a genus, species or
# vernacular (Cherax quadricarinatus iridovirus; signal crayfish associated hepe-like virus 1).
#   both  -- genus names and single-word vernaculars: they retrieve records AND appear in names.
#   name  -- terms that must NOT enter the query. "shrimp", "prawn", "decapod" and "penstyl"
#            would each pull in thousands of penaeid records and break the crayfish-only scope,
#            but they must be recognised in names so Decapod penstyldensovirus 1 and Shrimp
#            white spot syndrome virus stay in tier 1.
#   query -- terms safe to search that would never occur in a virus name: family and infraorder
#            names, multi-word vernaculars. No viral record in GenBank carries a crayfish FAMILY
#            name in its organism name, so the four family rows below are forward-looking safety
#            nets (they would catch a future /host="Cambaridae sp." deposit) and currently match
#            nothing; an OR clause that matches nothing cannot change the result set.

column4: name-only: keeps decapod-named viruses in tier 1 without pulling all shrimp viruses
